The Graduate Certificate in Community Planning (CP) is an online program that helps students develop core competencies in sustainable Community Planning.
Through this program, students will gain a foundation in the principles and practices of community planning and development, specifically in areas of land use and environmental planning.
The history of planning has many examples of environmental injustice, in which land use decisions have privileged some communities over others.
A commitment to anti-racism, inclusiveness, equity, as well as spatial and social justice perspectives is an integral part of a planning education.
Students can earn their certificate in four sessions, maximizing flexibility and convenience for career enhancement, leadership positions in the industry, and professional growth.
The Community Planning online certificate aligns with the University's commitment to urban initiative, community engagement and solving the world's most important challenges by equiping students with practical knowledge and understanding of how to plan for and enable equitable and sustainable communities.

This 4-course asychonous online graduate certificate also creates a learning opportunity for students who may not be able to attend graduate school in person on a full time basis, thereby creating a diverse learning opportunity (goal 3 of the URI Stragic Priority 2) and increase graduate student enrollment (goal 2 of Strategic Priority 2).
The impact of a working public better informed in values and strategies of community planning should contribute to healthier and more sustainable communities environmentally, socially and economically.
The online graduate Community Planning certificate will open doors for recent college graduates as well as working professionals; they will become eligible for positions and promotion in a growing job market.
By combining this online certificate with other stackable certificates such as Public Administration, MEM and GIS, students will be well equipped to engage in the significant planning challenges of our time.
Our department currently offers an in-person Graduate Certificate in Community Planning.
This proposed new program will be offered in the 7-week online format and require 4 classes with 3 required classes and one elective (12 credits).

Our existing Community Planning Graduate Certificate requires 5 courses to complete the certificate (15 or 16 credits).
The asychonous online certitificate is intended for a different student population from our in-person gradute certificate and provides somewhat different content.
The online certificate content is pragmatically planned to be useful for working professionals, adapted for online delivery, and geared towards working professionals who do not have prior knowledge of planning.
The purpose of the Certificate is to give these students a way to quickly and remotely attain a basic knowledge of planning, and to stack that knowledge with other certificates, such as Public Policy, Marine Affairs, GIS, etc.
By contrast, the full semester, in-person planning program encompasses a wide and in-depth disciplinary space, with opportunities to learn from in-person university relationships and pursue independent research, while still providing future planners with knowledge and tools for professional work.

The competition among MSM programs is intense, with a large number of institutions offering these degrees.
Programs strive to differentiate themselves by emphasizing unique curricular components such as leadership development modules, capstone projects, or global immersion experiences, which are designed to enhance employability and prepare graduates for management roles.
The rise of digital learning technologies has also led many institutions to offer MSM programs in online or hybrid formats, further increasing their reach and intensifying competition as geographic barriers to enrollment are reduced.
To stand out in a crowded market, programs often seek accreditation from prestigious bodies like AACSB, AMBA, or EQUIS and aim to secure favorable rankings from notable publications.
Many programs also forge partnerships with businesses and other organizations to help in curriculum development, provide real-world learning opportunities, and facilitate networking and job placements for graduates.

Recent trends in MSM programs include an increased emphasis on technology and analytics to integrate digital technologies in business, a focus on sustainability and social responsibility reflecting broader societal concerns, and more customizable and flexible learning paths to attract a diverse student body with varying needs and career goals.
Overall, the market for MSM programs remains robust, driven by their relevance, accessibility, and adaptability to market needs and educational technologies, though programs must continuously innovate and adapt to remain competitive.

COM 446 | Media Theory, Effective Fall 2025 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Examines major theoretical approaches to the study of media.

MKT 469 | Special Topics in Marketing, Effective Fall 2025 Allow to be repeated under different topics (3 crs.) Selected topics of current interest in marketing. (Lec. 3) Pre: MKT265(H) or by permission of instructor.
May be repeated for a maximum of 12 credits with change of topic.
Not for graduate credit.
MKT 475 | Digital Marketing: Analytics and Strategy, Effective Fall 2025 Change title, prerequisites (3 crs.) Analyze ways marketers adapt their strategies in digital environments.
Apply analytical skills, digital marketing tools, and tactics.

Develop strategies for digital marketing that help meet broad marketing objectives. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: MKT 265 or 265H or permission of instructor.
TMD 203 | Textile Science, Effective Fall 2025 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) The primary textile industry: fiber to finished fabric.
Textile fibers and their properties; yarns, fabric construction, dyeing, finishing, and printing. (Lec. 3) Pre: TMD123.
For TM or TMD majors admitted to the College of Business.
TMD 213 | Textile Science Laboratory, Effective Fall 2025 Change prerequisites (1 cr.) Laboratory exercises in fiber identification, fabric analysis and fabric performance testing, dyeing and finishing. (Lab. 2 ) Pre: TMD203.
For TM or TMD majors admitted to the College of Business.
TMD 225 | Apparel I, Effective Fall 2025 Change prerequisites (4 crs.) Principles of garment production as related to construction, fit, performance, quality, and cost.
Construction techniques, sizing, material evaluation and assembly management.
Quality analysis and introduction to computer-aided design. (Lec. 2, Lab. 4) Pre: TMD103G.

TMD 232 | Introduction to Retailing, Effective Fall 2025 Change title, description (3 crs.) A comprehensive study of retailing as an operating system.
Examination of the strategies and the organizational structure that support the retail system, including but not limited to fashion. (Lec. 3/Online)

TMD 333 | Digital Retail, Effective Fall 2025 Change title, description (3 crs.) A comprehensive study of e-commerce and digitalized practices in the retail industry, including but not limited to fashion.
In-depth analysis and competency development in critical aspects of e-commerce. (Lec. 3) Pre: TMD232.
COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCES: HDF 306 | Infant and Toddler Development, Effective Fall 2025 Change description, course credits (3 crs.) Explores typical development in first three years.
Focuses on diverse family/community contexts.
Integration of theory and research with experiential learning. (Lec. 3) Pre: HDF200; HDF major or Early Intervention Cert; or permission of instructor.
HDF 308 | Early Childhood Development, Effective Fall 2025 Change description, course credits, prerequisites (3 crs.) Examines the biopsychosocial development of young children and the contexts whereby development occurs.
Integration of theory and research with experiential learning. (Lec. 2, Practicum 1/Online 2, Practicum 1) Pre: HDF200 or PSY232; HDF major; or instructor permission.

HDF 310 | Middle Childhood and Adolescent Development, Effective Fall 2025 Change description, credits (3 crs.) Explores physical, psychological, social, and emotional growth and development during middle childhood and adolescence.
Integration of theory and research with experiential learning. (Lec. 3) Pre: HDF major and HDF201, or permission of instructor HDF 312 | Emerging and Early Adult Development, Effective Fall 2025 Change description, credits, method of instruction (3 crs.) Examines biopsychosocial development and well-being in emerging and early adulthood.
Focuses on diverse identities, intimate relationships, career growth, and brain health.
Integration of theory and research with experiential learning. (Lec. 3) Pre: HDF major and HDF 201, or permission of instructor HDF 314 | Later Adulthood Growth and Development, Effective Fall 2025 Change description, credits (3 crs).
This course examines aging and later adulthood with a focus on social, health, and economic opportunities and challenges.
This class involves integration of theory and research with experiential learning. (Lec. 3) Pre: HDF major and HDF 201, or permission of instructor.

HDF 418 | Personal Finance, Effective Fall 2025 Change prerequisite (3 crs.) Personal financial planning and decisions for attaining individual and family goals.
Factors that affect, protect, and enhance financial security. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: completion of 24 or more credits.
Not for graduate credit.

KIN 243 | Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries, Effective Summer 2025 Change description, create online version (3 crs.) Introduces concepts of injury prevention, recognition and management of athletic injuries, accelerated rehabilitation, and emergency management in athletic settings.
For students with interest in sports, fitness, and allied health careers. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: Open to kinesiology majors only or wi th permission of instructor.
PSY 384 | Cognitive Psychology, Effective Spring 2026 Change description, create online version (3 crs.) An examination of contemporary research and theories on mental activities.
Topics will include perception, pattern recognition, attention, memory, problem solving, language, consciousness, and artificial intelligence. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: PSY 113 and 301 or equivalent.

PSY 435 | Applied Methods in Psychological Research, Effective Fall 2025 Method of instruction (3 crs.) This course will provide a structured training experience addressing data management, statistical analysis, how to handle methodological problems, and interpretation of results for applied psychology research topics. (Lec. 3) Pre: Grades of C or higher in either STA308 or PSY200, and in PSY301, and PSY 434, or by permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.
NEW COURSES COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCES: HDF 495 | Child Development Center Independent Study, Effective Fall 2025 (1-3 crs.) Advanced work in child development and child development center operations under the supervision of faculty or directors of the University of Rhode Island Child Development Centers.
May be repeated for up to 9 credits. (Independent Study) Pre: HDF200 or PSY232, and permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.

COLLEGE OF PHARMACY: PHP 300 | Practical Calculations for the Pharmacist, Effective Summer 2025 (1 cr.) This course provides training on performing pharmaceutical calculations in both outpatient and inpatient settings for students starting Advanced Pharmacy Placement Experience (APPE) rotations or preparing for licensure.
This course will review techniques for performing clinical and practice -based calculations as one would encounter in professional practice.
This course will also review best practices to recognize and prevent calculation errors. (Online) Pre: Current or concurrent enrollment in PHC515, PharmD P3 or P4 student, or by permission of instructor.
GRADUATE SCHOOL OF OCEANOGRAPHY: OCG 309 | Coast-to-Coast Ocean Carbon, Effective Summer 2025 (4 crs.) Course focuses on physical, chemical, and biological oceanography with an emphasis on estuaries.
Students collect, analyze, and interpret data from major estuaries, applying findings to aquaculture, fisheries, ocean acidification, and carbon sequestration. (Lec. 3, Lab 1)

Faculty Senate Executive Committee Report #2024-2025-09 Motion Regarding Honors Representation in the Faculty Senate March 6, 2025 Faculty Senate Meeting MOTION - That the Honors Program gain representation in the Faculty Senate per the following: Over the last year, the Faculty Senate, through its standing and special committees, has worked with Honors to restructure the program, and continues to actively pursue an option that would create a University-Sponsored Institute to house Honors. Until such time as this Institute is created or Honors is otherwise restructured, it is important that the program be represented formally in the university’s shared governance structure. While the program is undergoing a significant transition, it seems prudent to have an Honors representative actively participating in meetings where the future of the program is being discussed. Analogous to the way that deans and other administrators serve as ex officio members of the Faculty Senate, i.e. without the right to vote, but with the right to make and second motions and participate in debate, the Faculty Senate Executive Committee proposes that that the Honors Program Director become an ex officio member of the Faculty Senate effective immediately. Inclusion of the Honors representative in the Faculty Senate is a temporary measure which shall expire at the end of the 2025-2026 academic year.

FACULTY SENATE LEGISLATION April 16, 2026 Graduate Council Report 2025-2026-6B At the April 6, 2026 meeting of the Graduate Council, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval.
Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation By The Faculty Senate PROGRAM MODIFICATIONS COLLEGE OF BUSINESS Professional Science Masters - PSM, Effective Spring 2027 The Professional Science Masters (PSM) program is a non-thesis graduate degree program that prepares students for leadership and management roles in science- and technology-driven organizations.
Housed in the College of Business, the PSM integrates advanced scientific or technical coursework with professional skills in leadership, project management, communication, and applied problem solving that are broadly applicable in rapidly evolving scientific fields.
This 30–33 credit interdisciplinary degree combines a graduate certificate in a science or technical field with professional business coursework and applied experiential learning.

Students develop practical interpersonal, leadership, communication, and critical thinking skills, and apply these competencies in real-world organizational and industry contexts.
The PSM requires the completion of a graduate certificate in a science field, and four professional courses, including at least one capstone/practicum, and an additional relevant graduate-level course(s) from the URI Online portfolio as elective with Program Director approval.
PSM program tracks that have been certified by the National Professional Science Master's Association should have Industry Advisory Boards and include an integrative, hands-on experiential learning project or applied internship.
The menu of professional courses includes BUS532, BUS506, BUS509, BUS515, MBA540, and BUS557 (MBA557).
Other online courses may be approved by the program director.
At least one 3-credit course must be a capstone/practicum.
